item.title: 7 Most Unforgettable Battles in Fantasy Books, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, not video games or prestige content.] Some fantasy battles stay with you forever, and these unforgettable clashes prove why.
item.content:encoded: From Robert Jordan and Steven Erikson to David Gemmell and George R.R. Martin, fantasy authors have spent decades imagining conflicts that test their characters' courage, reshape entire kingdoms, and leave readers picking their jaws up off the floor in the aftermath. Consider this the definitive ranking of fantasy fiction's greatest battles, highlighting the unforgettable clashes that set the standard for warfare.

item.title: 30 Years Later, Sean Connery's Secret James Bond Thriller Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait about free movie availability.] Michael Bay’s 1996 thriller The Rock is currently free to stream. 30 years later, its still an exciting ride.
item.content:encoded: Back in the 1990s, Michael Bay was really cooking. Before the slog that was 2001’s Pearl Harbor and his divisive Transformers movies that simultaneously hurt and enhanced his career by sidelining him for decades, Bay debuted as a director with a trio of really exciting movies that prioritized a fun experience for the viewer. First there was 1995’s Bad Boys, the Will Smith and Martin Lawrence buddy-cop film that became a popular franchise. He closed out the decade with the genre-defining end-of-the-world disaster filmArmageddon. And in between those two, he gave us a tightly crafted thriller that is currently free to stream (with ads) on Pluto TV.

item.title: 8 Best Science Fantasy Books of the 21st Century
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, not gaming or prestige content.] Break genre barriers with spacefaring necromancers and aliens employing goblins. Here are some of the best sci-fi fantasy books.
item.content:encoded: The legendary science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke once said, “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.” The lines between sci-fi and fantasy blur in popular entertainment franchises like Star Wars, Warhammer 40,000, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, as well as in classic book series like Dune and Dragonriders of Pern. If you’re looking for a new world to explore and can’t decide if you want it filled with spaceships or dragons, you don’t necessarily have to choose. Just pick something from this list of the best science fantasy books of the 21st century.

item.title: 29 years later, Homer’s Best ‘The Simpsons’ Quote is Still Pure Genius
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective (29 years later), not new content.] Homer Simpson’s best quote from The Simpsons came during season 8 and contains some profoubd wisdom
item.content:encoded: Personally, my favorite-ever quote from Homer Simpson came during season 4 of The Simpsons, in an episode named “Whacking Day.” The episode is about the citizens of Springfield celebrating a local holiday named Whacking Day, when they lure all the snakes in Springfield to the center of town and then beat them to death with baseball bats. Everyone loves this holiday except Lisa Simpson, who finds it to be cruel.

item.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Bully Quote Is Still Among the Wisest in Comic Strip History
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about vintage comic strip quote.] Moe was Calvin’s big dumb bully in Calvin and Hobbes. Here is his best quote from the beloved comic strip.
item.content:encoded: In the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin often defines his babysitter Rosalyn as his arch-nemesis. He regularly plots against her and tries to sabotage her relationship with her boyfriend. He even locked her out of the house once while she was babysitting him, which got him into big trouble with his parents.

item.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Is the Greatest Line in Sci-Fi History
item.dc:creator: Terry Terrones
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show; not substance-based news.] Captain Kirk's speech in 'Return to Tomorrow' says more about what Star Trek stands for than any other line in the original series.
item.content:encoded: Some lines of dialogue become so famous they stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context. The words have long since transcended their original context and permeated the pop culture zeitgeist.

item.title: 61 Years Later, Charlie Brown's Greatest Enemy Is Still an Undefeated 'Peanuts' Icon
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about comic strip; not Polygon's core focus.] Charlie Brown's only real arch-rival was a malevolent tree. Chomp chomp chomp.
item.content:encoded: Like many comics aimed at children, Charles Schulz's Peanuts doesn't have too many actual villains. It has a number of antagonists, such as Lucy Van Pelt, various other kids, or the impersonal cloud of failure that constantly hangs over Charlie Brown's head, but it's rare to see a genuinely malevolent force in Peanuts — with one exception.

item.title: George R.R. Martin’s 7 Best Non-Game of Thrones Books, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic-novel/book promo excerpt; not game-related content.] From antebellum Mississippi vampires to cat-loving space traders, George R.R. Martin’s best work goes far beyond Westeros and Game of Thrones.
item.content:encoded: George R.R. Martin will forever be associated with his book series, A Song of Ice and Fire, and HBO’s adaptation, Game of Thrones, but there's considerably more to his bibliography than scheming Lannisters, fire-breathing dragons, and the unending wait for The Winds of Winter. Long before Westeros became a cultural phenomenon, Martin was building a reputation as one of science fiction and fantasy's most imaginative voices, writing everything from supernatural mysteries and vampiric thrillers to sprawling space operas and intimate character dramas.

item.title: Gary Larson's 10 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective of old comic strip; filler content.] Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was at its greatest when it was really, really funny. That's why is these are his 10 best comics
item.content:encoded: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke. Because of its brevity, it's easy to trivialize the medium as simply the “funny papers,” a daily, disposable art form designed to pick you up after reading the actual news.

item.title: 9 Calvin and Hobbes Comics from the 1990s that Prove Bill Watterson is a Genius
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective of classic 1990s comic strip.] Calvin and Hobbes creator Bill Watterson is a genius. Here are nine comics which prove it.
item.content:encoded: Calvin and Hobbescreator Bill Watterson is a genius. Over the course of ten years spanning more than 3,000 comic strips, he developed two truly irresistible characters that are still beloved by millions. There was a lot behind the success of Calvin and Hobbes, but I think part of the reason why Watterson is still so widely respected is that he was an incredibly versatile artist who managed to do a lot of different things in an artform that can sometimes be limiting.

item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Horror classic streaming availability clickbait; retroactive content.] The supernatural horror film Poltergeist is on Pluto TV, though there's still a debate as to who directed it
item.content:encoded: Poltergeist, which became available to stream for free on Pluto TV on Nov. 1, follows an ordinary suburban family that begins to experience strange things in their home. Furniture and toys move on their own, a glass of milk shatters out of nowhere, and the youngest child in the family, 5-year-old Carol Anne (Heather O'Rourke), begins to communicate with beings through the television. At first, these events are dismissed, but during a thunderstorm one night, a tree outside the windows of the kids’ room crashes in and snatches the boy. Then, a portal opens in their closet, sucking Carol Anne into another dimension. With help from some paranormal investigators, the family tries everything to bring her back.

item.title: 53 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Sci-Fi History Is Still The Best Book Quote Of The 1970s
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old book; not game/horror/prestige film.] Roadside Picnic ends with one of science fiction’s most beautiful lines, a simple wish for happiness that still resonates more than 50 years later.
item.content:encoded: The canon of science-fiction literature is home to countless unforgettable endings, from 1984’s short but devastating retrospective ("He loved Big Brother") to The Three-Body Problem’s defiant reminder that humanity cannot be so easily wiped out. The best sci-fi endings don't offer comfortable closure. Instead, they reframe everything that came before. In their closing lines, great sci-fi novelists leave readers suspended in the aftermath, forced to stew in the terrifying logic of cold technology, the fragility of human nature, and the vast expanse of space.

But The Far Side introduced new characters and scenarios every single day.

item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Grand Theft Auto 6 features an enormous cast of characters. Here's who plays Jason, Lucia, and the rest of the major players.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6 has the longest story ever seen in a GTA game, which also means that it has an enormous cast of characters. Between rival faction leaders, radio station DJs, and fictional rappers, you're going to meet a whole lot of people in Leonida. And some of their voices might sound very familiar.

item.title: How Long Does It Take To Beat GTA 6?
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] GTA 6 has the biggest story in the series' history. Here's how long it will take you to beat it.
item.content:encoded: If you couldn't guess by its 210 GB file size, Grand Theft Auto 6 is gigantic. Rockstar's latest open-world game is stuffed to the brim with things to do and steal. It also sports the beefiest story of any GTA game to date. Jason and Lucia star in a sprawling crime epic that takes the couple all around the state of Leonida. While it's difficult to put a consistent hour count on a true 100% playthrough of GTA 6, we do know that you won't be able to binge it all in one long weekend.

item.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Miss Wormwood Quote Is Still Among the Smartest in Comic Strip History
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not a game.] Looking back at Miss Wormwood's best moments in Calvin and Hobbes
item.content:encoded: Bill Watterson walked a few different tightropes when he created Calvin and Hobbes, one of which involved Calvin's relationship with school. It would've been easy to make it simply antagonistic, with Calvin as the hero fighting back against the dark forces of educational conformity, a bit like a comic adaptation of Pink Floyd's "Another Brick in the Wall." Any number of later webcomics that were unsubtly inspired by Calvin and Hobbes went this way, at least at first.

item.title: 2026's Most Viral Movie with 97 Rotten Tomatoes Score Sets Streaming Date
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: [Filtered: Generic streaming availability announcement, not prestige content.] One of 2026's most-talked-about movies is arriving on streaming next week.
item.content:encoded: In recent years, Nathan Fielder has rightfully earned a place as one of the most provocative figures in modern comedy. Most recently, the actor, filmmaker, and pilot (it’s a long story) co-directed You Can See Everything, a three-hour, brain-bending documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her partner Billy Evans in the days before Holmes began her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors.
